key_insight: A role-aware ML framework quantifies the value of off-ball defensive movements by generating context-conditioned counterfactuals and measuring their effect on possession value, revealing coordinated contributions that traditional metrics miss.
problem_solved: Standard stats and possession-value models focus on on-ball events and average ghosting simulations, failing to capture tactical, coordinated off-ball defense and therefore underestimating individual and role-level defensive impact.
method: Use high-frequency player-tracking data with a possession-value (PV) model to measure attacker threat over time.
Train context-conditioned counterfactual trajectory generators (role-aware ghosting / imitation models) to simulate alternative off-ball behaviors consistent with tactical roles.
Compute marginal defensive value as the PV difference between actual and counterfactual scenarios and aggregate by role to assign credit.
impact: Provides a practical, interpretable way to evaluate and compare off-ball defensive contributions, enabling better feature design, model-based coaching insights, and reward signals for multi-agent learning or scouting workflows.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pitch plots: actual player trajectories vs role-conditioned counterfactuals with a PV change heatmap overlay
Pipeline diagram: tracking data → role assignment → conditional ghosting model → PV delta → role-level attribution
Bar/radar chart: marginal PV contribution per player grouped by defensive role
Sequence animation: defender cluster movements showing how coordinated displacement reduces opponent expected-goal/threat
paper_title: A Machine Learning Framework for Off Ball Defensive Role and Performance Evaluation in Football
paper_authors: Sean Groom, Shuo Wang, Francisco Belo, Axl Rice, Liam Anderson
